acceptance_criteria: `pub struct Cache { pub entries: BTreeMap<String, CacheEntry> }`, `pub struct CacheEntry { pub model_hash: String, pub bytes: Vec<u8> }`, a new field `Document::cache: Option<Cache>` and `Document::fresh_cache_file(&self, path: &str) -> Option<&[u8]>`, documented, as in spec §2.

`cache/index.json` is written through the canonical JSON writer with `cache_format: 1` and `entries` sorted by `path` in byte order, each with `model_hash`, `path` and `sha256` (`sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` of the bytes), as in spec §1. Writing the same document twice gives byte-identical output, in both the unpacked and the `.sltwx` form.

Round trip (spec §6 test 1): a document with a 3-byte `cache/body-b-1.brep`, a 1024-byte `cache/display.glb` and a small `thumbnail.png` survives `write_unpacked`/`read_unpacked` and `write_sltwx`/`read_sltwx` with every entry's bytes and `model_hash` equal.

A model edit makes the cache stale (spec §6 test 2): after `refresh_model_hash`, `fresh_cache_file` returns the bytes of every entry built with the current hash; after changing one parameter expression in `model`, it returns `None` for all of them while `cache` still holds all 3 entries.

Bad caches never return an error (spec §4, §6 tests 3–6), each with its own test: one flipped byte in an unpacked `cache/display.glb` drops only that entry; `cache/index.json` of `{`, of `[]` and of `{"cache_format": 2, "entries": []}` each read as `cache: None`; an entry path of `../x`, of `cache/index.json` or of `cache/a/b`, or a `sha256` without the `sha256:` prefix, drops only that entry; an unlisted `cache/extra.bin` is not read, and writing unpacked with `cache: Some(…)` removes it.
`cache: None` (spec §6 test 7): every existing golden file is still reproduced byte for byte, and an existing unpacked `cache/` folder is left untouched.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
